items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to motor vehicle repair shop exclusions
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S6667

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to motor vehicle
repair shop exclusions

PURPOSE:
To exclude repair shops whose activities primarily consist of
restoring, rebuilding or customizing specialty motor vehicles or
motor vehicles at least 25 years old.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
Paragraph (d) of subdivision 2 of section 398-b of the vehicle and
traffic law, as amended by chapter 21 of the laws of 1980, is amended
and a new paragraph (e) is added.

EXISTING LAW:
None.

JUSTIFICATION:
Businesses who restore and customize specialty collector's automobiles
should not be classified as a motor vehicle repair shop. These types
of businesses do not repair vehicles used for daily transportation
but rather restore classic cars close to their original look and
feel. The purpose of car restoration is not to keep the car running,
necessarily, but to undo decades of botched or temporary repairs or
modifications. These types of automobile repair should not be subject
to the requirements of the Motor Vehicle Repair Shop Act.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
New bill.

LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become law.
